_doc: THE REGISTER OF THE BOOKS THIS PROJECT HOLDS TEXT FOR. It exists for the same reason data/research/newspapers/corpus.json does: a quote is checked against a committed file, and the file has to be traceable back to the artifact it came out of or the check is circular. Each entry says what the book is, which source record grades it, where the deposit copy is and its sha256, what derived text is committed and its sha256, how that text was produced, and what has actually been read out of it. A book with no entry here has no committed text; an entry whose sha256 no longer matches means somebody edited a transcription, which is the one thing this subtree must never do. DERIVED TEXT IS COMMITTED, SCANS AND RENDERS ARE NOT: the deposit under chicago/reference/ is read-only and nothing here is published.

books.title: The Autobiography of Gurdon Saltonstall Hubbard, Pa-pa-ma-ta-be, "The Swift Walker"
books.imprint: Chicago: R. R. Donnelley & Sons Company, The Lakeside Press, Christmas 1911 — The Lakeside Classics

text.how: curl -L https://archive.org/download/autobiographyofg00hubb/autobiographyofg00hubb_djvu.txt on 2026-09-03, committed byte for byte. The identifier was confirmed against archive.org's advancedsearch API first (numFound 1, year 1911).
text.corroborated_by: pdftotext -layout over the deposited PDF's own embedded text layer, an independent extraction of the same scan, which agrees with the committed text to better than 0.9999 on whitespace-normalised comparison. The two differ only where poppler welds an italic word to its neighbour.

page_index.why: THE COMMITTED TEXT HAS NO PAGE BREAKS. The Internet Archive's djvu output carries not one form feed and prints no folio of its own, so the leaf boundaries are transferred onto it from the deposited PDF's text layer, which has all 226. 207 of the 208 non-blank leaves aligned; the one that did not is the Contents at leaf 19, whose columns poppler reorders, and it is declared as such.

books.read: Pages ix-xxvii and 27-41, 135-138, 141-144, 153-159, 165-174, 178-182, declared item by item in coverage.json. Pages 1-26, 42-134, 139-140, 145-152, 160-164, 175-177 are NOT read and are not declared: they are Montreal, Mackinaw and the Illinois River posts, and they name no Chicago.
books.note: THE SCAN IS OUT OF ORDER. Pages xv and xvi were photographed at the front of the Internet Archive item, as leaves 11 and 12, ahead of the title page. The text proves it and six folios read off the page confirm it; tools/build_book_page_index.py carries the three folio runs that forces and hard-fails if a printed folio ever contradicts them.

books.title: Henry H. Hurlbut, Chicago Antiquities (Chicago, 1881), pages 28-36 — the chapter on the American Fur Company and Chicago

text.how: Copied byte-identical from this project's own genealogytrails cache, itself fetched 2026-09-03 for T-0556. NOBODY IN THIS PROJECT HAS SEEN THE BOOK; what is held is a 2006 web transcription of nine of its pages.

books.read: Pages 28-36, declared in coverage.json as ONE `list` item and not as nine `page` items, because the transcription marks no page breaks and this project will not invent them.
books.note: Registered here retrospectively by T-0501, which is the pass that gave this domain a corpus at all. Nothing about the T-0575 reading is changed by the entry.

books.title: Fergus' Historical Series, Nos. 26-29 — No. 26, Harrison's A Discourse on the Aborigines of the Ohio Valley; No. 27, Beckwith's The Illinois and Indiana Indians; No. 28, Fergus's Directory of the City of Chicago for 1843; No. 29, Kirby's Biographical Sketch of Joseph Duncan
books.imprint: Chicago: Fergus Printing Company, 1883-1888 — four numbers bound in one volume (Allen County Public Library copy)

text.how: The deposit's own hOCR search text, copied BYTE FOR BYTE by tools/build_fergus_page_index.py --build on 2026-09-03. Not cleaned, not re-flowed, not re-OCR'd. The deposit was already in the repository and nothing was fetched for it; the archive.org _djvu.txt was deliberately NOT used, because the deposit's page index addresses THIS text and swapping texts would break every locator in the domain.

page_index.why: NOT AN ALIGNMENT — A TRANSCRIPTION OF THE SCANNER'S OWN INDEX. Unlike Hubbard's autobiography, whose committed text carries no page breaks at all, this deposit ships fergushistorical2629unse_hocr_pageindex.json: 858 entries of exact character offsets into the search text, one per scanned leaf. The tool turns those offsets into 1-based line numbers, assigns each leaf to one of the volume's four numbers from the four title pages read off the scan, and reads the printed folio out of the running head where the OCR gives it.

books.claims: chicago/4d/data/research/books/claims/fergus_26_29_second_half.json — 58 claims, T-0500 (leaves 430-858). The first half, leaves 1-429, is T-0499.
books.read: Leaves 430-858, declared in five items in coverage.json: the 1843 Business Directory (430-457) and Obituary (606-644) and the whole of Fergus No. 29 (658-850) read in full; the publisher's advertisement leaves (645-657, 851-858) read for Chicago titles only; the 1843 alphabetical name directory (458-605) SWEPT BY MACHINE and not read continuously, which its own declaration states. Leaves 1-429 are T-0499's.
books.note: FOUR PAMPHLETS IN ONE COVER AND FOUR SEPARATE FOLIO SEQUENCES. Every number restarts its page numbering at 1, so a printed folio in this volume is meaningless without its `part`, and the page index carries both. The folio offset is not even constant WITHIN a number — an inserted plate shifts it — so the read folios are grouped into runs of a single offset and a leaf between two runs keeps printed_page null rather than being guessed at. Thirty-three folio readings that contradict every run are discarded and listed, the commonest being the directory's own running head, 'CHICAGO DIRECTORY, 1 843.', whose year reads as a page number.
